obligations.summary: The provider shall draw up a written, machine-readable, physical or electronically signed EU declaration of conformity for each high-risk AI system and keep it available to national competent authorities for 10 years after the system has been placed on the market or put into service.
The provider shall submit a copy of the EU declaration of conformity to the relevant national competent authorities upon request.

The EU declaration of conformity shall state that the high-risk AI system meets the requirements of Section 2, contain all information set out in Annex V, and be translated into a language easily understood by the national competent authorities of the Member States where the system is placed on the market or made available.

Where high-risk AI systems are subject to other Union harmonisation legislation also requiring an EU declaration of conformity, a single EU declaration of conformity shall be drawn up covering all applicable Union law, containing all information necessary to identify each piece of legislation to which it relates.
By drawing up the EU declaration of conformity, the provider assumes responsibility for compliance with the requirements of Section 2 and shall keep the declaration up-to-date as appropriate.
